Sold as: MCP3004-I/P bare chip in a DIP-14 package (pins 1-4 CH0-CH3, 5-6 NC, 7 DGND, 8 CS/SHDN, 9 DIN, 10 DOUT, 11 CLK, 12 AGND, 13 VREF, 14 VDD), plugged straight into a breadboard.

pins.name: CH0
pins.description: Analog input 0 (pin 1), 0 V to VREF; never above VDD + 0.6 V

pins.name: CH1
pins.description: Analog input 1 (pin 2), 0 V to VREF; never above VDD + 0.6 V

pins.name: CH2
pins.description: Analog input 2 (pin 3), 0 V to VREF; never above VDD + 0.6 V

pins.name: CH3
pins.description: Analog input 3 (pin 4), 0 V to VREF; never above VDD + 0.6 V

pins.name: CS/SHDN
pins.description: Chip select / shutdown, active low (pin 8). Must go high between conversions

pins.name: DIN
pins.description: Serial data in: start bit, SGL/DIFF and channel bits (pin 9)

pins.name: DOUT
pins.description: Serial data out: null bit then the 10-bit result (pin 10)

pins.name: CLK
pins.description: Serial clock, 10 kHz to 1.35 MHz at 2.7 V, 3.6 MHz at 5 V (pin 11)

pins.name: VREF
pins.description: Reference voltage input (pin 13): sets full scale. Tie to VDD (3.3 V) for 0-3.3 V inputs

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Supply, 2.7-5.5 V (pin 14). Use 3.3 V with an ESP32/Pico so DOUT stays at 3.3 V logic

buildNotes: Send 3 bytes in SPI mode 0: 0x01, 0x80 | (ch << 4), 0x00 (single-ended). The result is (reply[1] & 0x03) << 8 | reply[2]; the top bits of reply[1] are undefined (high-Z, then the null bit).
Pull CS/SHDN high after every conversion: each conversion starts with a new CS falling edge.
Volts = code x VREF / 1024. Tie VREF to VDD (3.3 V) for a 0-3.3 V range, or to a precision reference for better accuracy.
Power it from 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico; at 5 V DOUT would drive 5 V into a 3.3 V GPIO.
Keep SPI clock between 10 kHz and 1.35 MHz at 2.7-3.3 V (3.6 MHz max at 5 V); too slow and the sample capacitor droops.
Put a 1 uF ceramic capacitor from VDD to AGND close to the chip and join AGND and DGND at one point.
Pins 5 and 6 are not connected inside the chip; leave them open.

driver.code:
# MCP3004 4-channel 10-bit SPI ADC (Microchip MCP3004/3008, DS21295D), MicroPython driver.
# Uses the datasheet's 3-byte, 8-bit-aligned transfer (Section 6.1, Figure 6-1, SPI mode 0,0):
#   byte 0: 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 START
#   byte 1: SGL/DIFF D2 D1 D0 x x x x   (D2 is "don't care" on the MCP3004, sent as 0)
#   byte 2: x x x x x x x x
# Reply: byte 1 = ? ? ? ? ? NULL B9 B8, byte 2 = B7..B0.
# Code = 1024 * VIN / VREF (Equation 4-2).
from machine import Pin


class MCP3004:
    def __init__(self, spi, cs, vref=3.3):
        """spi: machine.SPI in mode 0 (polarity=0, phase=0), 10 kHz to 1.35 MHz at 2.7 V
        (3.6 MHz max at 5 V). cs: GPIO number of CS/SHDN. vref: voltage on the VREF pin."""
        self.spi = spi
        self.cs = Pin(cs, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.vref = vref
        self._tx = bytearray(3)
        self._rx = bytearray(3)

    def read_raw(self, channel, single_ended=True):
        """Convert one channel and return the 10-bit code (0-1023).
        single_ended=False selects the pseudo-differential pair (Table 5-1)."""
        if not 0 <= channel <= 3:
            raise ValueError('MCP3004 channel must be 0-3')
        self._tx[0] = 0x01  # seven leading zeros, then the start bit
        self._tx[1] = (0x80 if single_ended else 0x00) | ((channel & 0x03) << 4)
        self._tx[2] = 0x00
        self.cs.value(0)
        self.spi.write_readinto(self._tx, self._rx)
        self.cs.value(1)  # CS must go high between conversions (tCSH >= 270 ns)
        return ((self._rx[1] & 0x03) << 8) | self._rx[2]

    def raw_to_volts(self, raw):
        return raw * self.vref / 1024

    def read_volts(self, channel, single_ended=True):
        return self.raw_to_volts(self.read_raw(channel, single_ended))

example.code:
from machine import Pin, SPI
import time
from mcp3004 import MCP3004

spi = SPI(1, baudrate=1000000, polarity=0, phase=0, sck=Pin({CLK}), mosi=Pin({DIN}), miso=Pin({DOUT}))
adc = MCP3004(spi, {CS_SHDN}, vref=3.3)  # VREF tied to 3.3 V
while True:
    r0 = adc.read_raw(0)
    r2 = adc.read_raw(2)
    print('CH0=%d %.3fV CH2=%d %.3fV' % (r0, adc.raw_to_volts(r0), r2, adc.raw_to_volts(r2)))
    time.sleep(1)

# MCP3004 4-channel 10-bit SPI ADC (MCP3004)

## Overview
The **MCP3004** from Microchip is a 10-bit SAR analog-to-digital converter with 4 single-ended inputs (or 2 pseudo-differential pairs) and an SPI interface, up to 200 ksps at 5 V (75 ksps at 2.7 V). Hobbyists buy the bare **MCP3004-I/P in a DIP-14 package** and plug it straight into a breadboard. It is the 4-channel sibling of the MCP3008 and uses the same command frame.

## Pinout (DIP-14, pin 1 next to the notch)
| Pin | Name | Function |
|---|---|---|
| 1-4 | CH0-CH3 | Analog inputs, 0 V to VREF |
| 5, 6 | NC | Not connected |
| 7 | DGND | Digital ground |
| 8 | CS/SHDN | Chip select / shutdown, active low |
| 9 | DIN | SPI data in (MOSI) |
| 10 | DOUT | SPI data out (MISO) |
| 11 | CLK | SPI clock |
| 12 | AGND | Analog ground |
| 13 | VREF | Reference voltage input (full scale) |
| 14 | VDD | Supply, 2.7-5.5 V |

## Electrical limits
- Supply: 2.7-5.5 V; about 425 uA running at 5 V (225 uA at 2.7 V), 5 nA standby.
- Inputs: VSS to VREF for valid codes; never more than VDD + 0.6 V or below -0.6 V.
- SPI clock: 1.35 MHz max at VDD 2.7 V, 3.6 MHz at 5 V; keep it above about 10 kHz so the sample doesn't droop.
- Source impedance: high-impedance sources need a slower clock or a buffer (datasheet Section 4.1).

## Interface details
- SPI mode 0,0 (or 1,1), MSB first. Each conversion starts on a CS falling edge; CS must go high between conversions.
- Datasheet 8-bit-aligned transfer (Figure 6-1), 3 bytes:
  - send `0x01`, `0x80 | (ch << 4)`, `0x00` for single-ended channel ch (`ch << 4` without 0x80 for pseudo-differential, Table 5-1);
  - receive: byte 1 = `? ? ? ? ? 0 B9 B8`, byte 2 = `B7..B0`, so code = `(rx[1] & 0x03) << 8 | rx[2]`.
- Code = 1024 x VIN / VREF (Equation 4-2); volts = code x VREF / 1024.

## Wiring
- ESP32: VDD and VREF -> 3V3, AGND and DGND -> GND, CLK -> D18, DOUT -> D19, DIN -> D23, CS/SHDN -> D5.
- Pico: VDD and VREF -> 3V3(OUT), AGND and DGND -> GND, CLK -> GP18, DOUT -> GP16, DIN -> GP19, CS/SHDN -> GP17.
- Raspberry Pi 4: VDD and VREF -> pin 1 (3.3 V), grounds -> pin 6, CLK -> pin 23, DOUT -> pin 21, DIN -> pin 19, CS/SHDN -> pin 24 (CE0).
- 1 uF ceramic from VDD to AGND right at the chip. Leave pins 5 and 6 unconnected.

## Using the driver
```python
from machine import Pin, SPI
from mcp3004 import MCP3004
spi = SPI(1, baudrate=1000000, polarity=0, phase=0, sck=Pin(18), mosi=Pin(23), miso=Pin(19))
adc = MCP3004(spi, 5, vref=3.3)
raw = adc.read_raw(0)
print('CH0=%d %.3fV' % (raw, adc.raw_to_volts(raw)))
```

## Gotchas
- Powered at 5 V, DOUT swings to 5 V: run it from 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico.
- Mask the reply: only the low two bits of the second byte are data (the rest are high-Z and the null bit).
- VREF sets the scale; if it isn't tied to anything, readings are garbage.
- If it was powered up with CS low, CS must go high and low again before the first conversion.
- Only channels 0-3 exist; MCP3008 code asking for CH4-CH7 reads CH0-CH3 again (D2 is ignored).
